strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates the challenge of unreliable teacher guidance under domain shifts with concrete motivation
Universal framework: Demonstrates applicability across three diverse domains (image classification, RL, autonomous driving) with minimal modifications

Interesting experimental insights: The case where teachers significantly underperform (Level 2 domain shift) effectively shows AUKT can extract value from weak teachers, distinguishing it from prior work
Comprehensive baseline evaluation: Compares against four knowledge transfer methods across multiple architectures (ResNet, VGG, ShuffleNet, MobileNet, WRN)
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations that clearly communicate the core ideas
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution is a straightforward application of existing CP to existing KD via simple adaptive weighting (Eq. 2). Adding a learned weight function w(x) to existing losses is incremental

Weak theoretical justification: Appendix A.2 analysis is shallow—gradient modulation is standard, critical point analysis only covers MSE losses, and lacks formal justification for why CP-based uncertainty should outperform alternatives. Theory doesn't leverage CP's coverage guarantees

Fundamental mismatch between CP assumptions and problem: CP requires calibration and test data from the same distribution, but paper tackles domain shifts (P_T ≠ P_S). CP's coverage guarantees degrade under shift; this inconsistency is not adequately addressed

Critical missing ablations: No comparison with other uncertainty methods (entropy, Bayesian, MC Dropout); no ablation on weighting function design (why hard thresholding vs. soft?); no sensitivity analysis on α and λ parameters; no investigation of calibration set size effects

Lack of statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Improvements in Table 1 (0.3-1.0%) are modest and could be noise. Table 4 shows trivial improvements (0.03%). No multiple runs with standard deviations

Ad-hoc design choices: Weighting functions use hard binary thresholds (w=1 if u_T=0 else 0) without principled justification or ablation. Different domains use different weighting schemes without explanation. Soft RL variant appears ad-hoc with unexplained temperature parameter

Limited domain shift realism: All domain shifts are artificial (Gaussian noise added to 30-40% of images). Real distribution shifts (weather, lighting, viewpoint, sensor type) are more complex. Results may not generalize to natural shifts

Incomplete related work comparison: Missing recent domain-adaptive knowledge distillation methods; no comparison with other uncertainty-aware transfer approaches; baselines mostly from 2014-2018; doesn't compare fixed vs. adaptive weighting designs from prior work

Limited RL evaluation: Only simple gridworld environments with discrete, fully observable spaces. No comparison with other uncertainty-aware RL methods. Absolute rewards in Lava 2 remain modest despite large percentage improvements

Insufficient autonomous driving evaluation: Only one dataset (SullyChen); artificial domain shifts (Gaussian noise); no comparison with domain-adaptive steering methods; no test on realistic sensor shifts
